what.quote: 3.1.2.1 The proper shipping name is that portion of the entry most accurately describing the goods in the Dangerous Goods List, which is shown in upper case characters (plus any numbers, Greek letters, "sec", "tert", and the letters m, n, o, p, which form an integral part of the name). An alternative proper shipping name may be shown in brackets following the main proper shipping name [e.g., ETHANOL (ETHYL ALCOHOL)]. Portions of an entry appearing in lower case need not be considered as part of the proper shipping name but may be used.
what.citation: UN Model Regulations Rev.24 (ST/SG/AC.10/1/Rev.24), Vol. I, 3.1.2.1

choices.quote: 3.1.2.2 When a combination of several distinct proper shipping names are listed under a single UN number, and these are separated by "or" in lower case or are punctuated by commas, only the most appropriate shall be shown in the transport document and package marks.
choices.citation: UN Model Regulations Rev.24 (ST/SG/AC.10/1/Rev.24), Vol. I, 3.1.2.2

spelling.quote: 3.1.2.3 Proper shipping names may be used in the singular or plural as appropriate. In addition, when qualifying words are used as part of the proper shipping name, their sequence on documentation or package marks is optional. For instance, "DIMETHYLAMINE AQUEOUS SOLUTION" may alternatively be shown "AQUEOUS SOLUTION OF DIMETHYLAMINE".
spelling.citation: UN Model Regulations Rev.24 (ST/SG/AC.10/1/Rev.24), Vol. I, 3.1.2.3
